name: EU legal baseline for the digital product passport (ESPR Chapter III, Batteries Regulation Arts 77-78, registry act 2026/1778, sectoral passports)
scope_note: Covers the minimum DPP method that binding EU law prescribes as of 2026-10-19: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR) Arts 2, 9 to 16, 27, 29 to 31, 41, 42 and Annex III; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Arts 13(6)-(9), 77, 78 and Annexes VI Part C and XIII (consolidated version of 2026-08-13); Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 (registry) in full; Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736 (bibliographic annex only); the passport provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 (construction products, Arts 75 to 80), Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 (toys, Arts 19 to 24), Regulation (EU) 2026/405 (detergents, Arts 19 to 25) and Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 (vehicles, Art. 13). It also records non-binding Commission material (general DPP FAQ v1.0, battery FAQ, registry user guide v1.03, registry and timeline pages) and the February 2024 draft of the standardisation request M/604, each marked as non-binding or draft. It leaves out: the content of any EN, ISO or IEC standard (bibliographic metadata only); technology choices such as GS1 Digital Link, AAS, verifiable credentials, dataspaces or ledgers (other method files describe them as deltas); product-group data sets under ESPR Art. 4 (none adopted); the passport-like provisions of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation and the Critical Raw Materials Act (named in the Commission FAQ table, not examined); Annex VI of the toy and detergent regulations (data lists not read); the Data Act and eIDAS beyond the points that Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 references.
summary: EU law does not prescribe a DPP technology; it prescribes properties, roles and one central component. A passport is a product-specific data set reached through a data carrier that is physically on the product, its packaging or documents, and that links to a persistent unique product identifier which also enables a web link to the passport (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Arts 2(28)-(30) and 10(1)). Passport data stays decentralised: the economic operator, or a DPP service provider acting for it, stores the passport, and under the ESPR a back-up copy must also be held by a DPP service provider (Arts 10(4) and 11(c)). The data must be based on open standards, interoperable, machine-readable, structured, searchable and transferable without vendor lock-in, and the system must guarantee authentication, reliability, integrity, security and privacy (Arts 10(1)(d) and 11). Access is tiered by actor according to access rights that product-group acts define; the Batteries Regulation already fixes three tiers in Annex XIII (public; notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission; persons with a legitimate interest), but the implementing act that defines legitimate interest (Art. 77(9)) is still not adopted. The one central component is the Commission's DPP registry (ESPR Art. 13), specified by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778: verified economic operators register each passport through a web interface or an API; the registry checks semantic conformity, granularity, commodity code and the back-up link, stores identifiers and registrant data, and returns a persistent registration identifier. Customs will verify that identifier and the commodity code against the registry, automatically once the registry is interconnected with EU CSW-CERTEX (due within four years of the registry act's entry into force). Operator verification uses eIDAS means: qualified electronic signatures or seals, electronic identification at assurance level high, or electronic attestations of attributes; the Commission's user guide shows PAdES-sealed PDF declarations. The registry also hosts a semantic repository of versioned, machine-readable data models with DCAT-AP metadata, which becomes the authoritative data model source for passports. A public web portal (Art. 14) is required but not yet launched. Lifecycle rules require accuracy and updates, links from a new passport to the original one, availability through the required period even after the operator's insolvency, and, for batteries, transfer of responsibility on repurposing or remanufacturing and the end of the passport after recycling. As of 2026-10-19 the only passport that has a fixed start date is the battery passport (2027-02-18); ESPR passports wait for product delegated acts (none adopted), construction, toy and detergent passports wait for their own delegated or implementing acts and dates of application, and the vehicle circularity passport starts in 2032. The Commission's user guide states that battery passport registration is not yet possible because the semantic catalogue for that product group is not defined.

maturity.spec_status: Binding EU law in force. ESPR DPP duties are dormant until an Art. 4 delegated act applies (none adopted as of 2026-10-19). Battery passport mandatory from 2027-02-18. maturity.adoption_evidence: The registry is live (Commission news and registry page; production host registry.product-passport.ec.europa.eu and test host registry.acc.product-passport.ec.europa.eu named in documentation; neither contacted). The registry user guide v1.03 (2026-09-16) says only the product group 'Batteries' is selectable, only item level is available, and successful battery registration is not yet possible because the semantic catalogue for the group is not defined. No ESPR product group has an applicable passport duty. No official count of registered passports was found. The web portal (Art. 14) is described by the Commission FAQ as planned for the coming years.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: This file is the baseline. Every other method file states its delta against it. Presumption of conformity with ESPR Arts 10 and 11 follows from the six harmonised standards cited by Decision (EU) 2026/1736 to the extent they cover the requirements (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 41(2)); that decision is adopted under the ESPR only, so it gives no presumption for battery passports under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. Common specifications (ESPR Art. 42) are a fallback that the Commission has not used.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Three identifier classes are defined in law. (1) Unique product identifier: a unique character string that identifies a product and also enables a web link to the passport (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 2(30)); for batteries, a unique string that identifies the battery and enables a web link to the battery passport, attributed by the economic operator that places the battery on the market (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Arts 3(1)(66) and 77(3)). (2) Unique operator identifier and (3) unique facility identifier (ESPR Art. 2(31) and (33); Annex III points (g), (h), (i), (k)). The product identifier must be persistent and linked to the passport through the data carrier (ESPR Art. 10(1)(a)). Identifier and carrier must comply with ISO/IEC 15459-1:2014, -2:2015, -3:2014, -4:2014, -5:2014 and -6:2014 or equivalent European or international standards until harmonised-standard references are published in the OJ (ESPR Arts 10(1)(c), 12(1), Annex III second paragraph); the battery passport keeps its own reference to the same six parts 'or their equivalent' (Batteries Art. 77(3)). Annex III also lists a Global Trade Identification Number (point (c)) and the importer's EORI number (point (j)). Where an operator or facility identifier does not exist, the economic operator that creates or updates the passport requests one on that actor's behalf after confirming none exists (ESPR Art. 12(2)-(3)). The registry adds a fourth identifier: a unique, persistent registration identifier that the registry generates and returns after a successful registration (ESPR Art. 13(5); Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(8) and (10)). Granularity: model, batch or item as the product-group act sets; item-level registrations link to batch and model identifiers where these exist, batch-level to a model identifier (2026/1778, Art. 8(1)-(5)). Toy and detergent passports must use identical product, operator and registration identifiers where another Union act also requires a passport (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 21(3); Regulation (EU) 2026/405, Art. 23). Non-binding concretisation: the registry user guide v1.03 requires the 'Unique Product Identifier (UPI)' to be a URL starting with https://, at most 2000 characters, that resolves to where the passport data is hosted; optional fields 'Model Identifier' and 'Batch Identifier'; it calls the returned registration identifier 'URI (Unique Registration Identifier)'. The law sets no identifier syntax of its own; the ISO/IEC 15459 series and EN 18219:2026 are recorded bibliographically only.

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: The payload decoded from the carrier; whether it is an https URL of at most 2000 characters (registry rule); whether two products share an identifier; the identifier value inside the resolved passport; the registration identifier shown in an operator-supplied proof of registration or registration export.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: A data carrier is a linear bar code symbol, a two-dimensional symbol or another automatic identification data capture medium that a device can read (ESPR Art. 2(29)). It must be physically present on the product, its packaging or accompanying documentation as the delegated act specifies (ESPR Art. 10(1)(b)); each delegated act sets the carrier type, layout and position (Art. 9(2)(b)-(c)); labels must include carriers where appropriate (Art. 16(4)); digital instructions must be reachable through the carrier (Art. 27(7)). The economic operator must give dealers and online marketplaces a digital copy of the carrier or the product identifier, free of charge, promptly and in any event within five working days of a request (Art. 10(3)). Batteries: from 2027-02-18 every battery bears a QR code per Annex VI Part C; for LMT, industrial above 2 kWh and EV batteries it gives access to the passport (Batteries Art. 13(6)); the QR code is printed or engraved visibly, legibly and indelibly on the battery, or on packaging and accompanying documents where size or nature prevents it (Art. 13(7)); Annex VI Part C asks only for high contrast and a size that a common QR reader in a hand-held device reads easily, and names no symbology standard; Art. 13(8) allows delegated acts for alternative smart labels; Art. 13(9) requires new markings after re-use, repurposing or remanufacturing. Toys: carrier on the toy or an affixed label, otherwise on packaging or documents; visible before purchase including distance sales; one carrier when several Union acts need one (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 19(7)-(8)). Detergents: carrier printed or attached to label, packaging or bulk documents, indelible, machine-readable, with a 'scan for more information' type statement, also at refill stations (Regulation (EU) 2026/405, Art. 21). Construction products: carrier placed as Art. 18(2)(g) requires (Regulation (EU) 2024/3110, Art. 77(1)). Non-binding: the Commission DPP FAQ (Q26) says QR codes and NFC are being assessed and the delegated act will fix the carrier. The M/604 draft annex (Part B point 2) asked for rules on symbology, encoding, error correction, print and durability, a link to public and restricted passport data, optional control data (for example a hash of the registered passport) and optional offline basic data elements.

L02_data_carriers.observable_black_box: An image or tag of the carrier as a sample artifact: whether it decodes, what payload it carries, whether the payload leads to the passport; the digital copy given to a dealer and the time to supply it (process evidence, not a protocol observable).

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: The law names no protocol, HTTP method, header or media type. It requires that the unique identifier enables a web link to the passport (ESPR Art. 2(30); Batteries Art. 3(1)(66)); that passport data be transferable through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in (ESPR Art. 10(1)(d); Batteries Art. 77(5)); and full interoperability with other passports on technical, semantic and organisational aspects of end-to-end communication and data transfer (ESPR Art. 11(a); Batteries Art. 78(a); toys Art. 20(1); detergents Art. 22; CPR Art. 78(a)). Toy and detergent passports must be accessible to consumers without registration or a password (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 20(4); Regulation (EU) 2026/405, Art. 22). Non-binding concretisation by the registry: the UPI must be an https URL that resolves to the hosted passport data; the registry rejects a UPI that is malformed, uses an unsupported protocol, points to a disallowed domain or a non-permitted port (error 'The UPI URL is invalid'), that cannot be resolved (error code NOT_RESOLVABLE_UPI shown in the guide), or whose resolution involves excessive redirects, a redirect to a less secure protocol, or an oversized response (registry user guide v1.03, Ch. 6.2.1-6.2.2). The M/604 draft annex (Part B point 5) asked for standards on data exchange protocols between two or more parties and on processes to introduce, modify and update passport data; EN 18216:2026 is the cited result (bibliographic only).

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: Law requires passport data to be searchable (ESPR Art. 10(1)(d); Batteries Art. 77(5)) and the Commission to run a public web portal for searching and comparing passport data within access rights (ESPR Art. 14; CPR Art. 79(3)). No API is prescribed for the economic operator's passport host. The only API in binding law is the registry's: an application programming interface for registering passports and receiving registry information (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 3(b)); registration is made through the secure user interface or the API, and the registration identifier is returned in the interface or the API response, depending on the channel (Art. 8(6), (10)); the semantic repository offers publicly documented APIs free of charge (Art. 12). Non-binding: the user guide v1.03 documents the web channel only: a single-passport form or a JSON or XML file upload of at most 100 passports and 1 GB, with downloadable template.json and template.xml; each request receives a correlation ID; statuses PROCESSING, SUCCESS, FAILURE; one invalid passport rejects the whole file; results exportable as CSV. The resources page section 'DPP Registry technical guidelines' holds no file yet ('New files will be uploaded soon'), so no registry API specification is public. The battery FAQ says registration can use an API, manual entry or bulk upload. The M/604 draft annex (Part B point 8) asked that custodians of passports (economic operators or service providers) offer APIs for create, read, update and delete operations and for remote queries from the registry or national authorities, covering syntax and semantics, security and access control, performance, versioning, message exchange patterns, availability and data authenticity; EN 18222:2026 is the cited result (bibliographic only).

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Content is set per product group: ESPR Annex III is a menu (points (a) to (l): information under Art. 7, unique product identifier, GTIN, commodity codes such as TARIC, compliance documents, manuals and safety information, manufacturer and other operator identifiers, facility identifiers, importer data with EORI, the responsible Union operator under Art. 4 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, and a reference to the DPP service provider hosting the back-up), plus a third paragraph on voluntary ecodesign information such as the EU Ecolabel; each delegated act chooses the binding set (Art. 9(2)(a)). Manufacturer and importer name, trade name or mark, postal address and electronic contact go on the public part of the passport where applicable (Arts 27(6)(a), 29(3)(a)). Batteries: Annex XIII fixes four groups: point 1 public model data items (a)-(s); point 2 model data for persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission items (a)-(d); point 3 test report results for notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission; point 4 individual-battery data for persons with a legitimate interest items (a)-(d), including status values original, repurposed, re-used, remanufactured or waste. Items follow the application dates of their source articles (for example carbon footprint and recycled content depend on acts not yet adopted). Construction products: declaration of performance and conformity, product information, technical documentation, label, unique identifiers and carriers of key parts (CPR Art. 76(2)(a)). Vehicles: Art. 13(2) list (removal information, derogated substances, recycled content declaration, spare parts catalogue). Format rules: open standards, interoperable, machine-readable, structured, searchable (ESPR Art. 10(1)(d)). The registry act introduces common semantics: passport data must follow common, versioned data models in the semantic repository, derived from delegated acts or other Union law (2026/1778, Art. 11); the repository holds attribute meanings, specifications for typed resolvable links between passports and evidence, data models and formats per product, DCAT-AP metadata, role meanings, and multilingual labels, with search and public APIs, free of charge (Art. 12). 'Semantic conformity' means all required elements are present, all elements meet their structure, format, value type and vocabulary rules, and elements can be interpreted through the repository (Art. 2(12)). Non-binding: the user guide says passport data follows one of the pre-defined schemas in XML or JSON, at minimum the required attributes and at most required plus optional attributes of the authoritative schema; the battery FAQ calls the repository a rulebook used to check semantic completeness and says non-applicable fields are left out of the models (Q7.6, Q11.1). Voluntary data is allowed if clearly separated from mandatory data (FAQ Q22; toys Art. 19(10); detergents Art. 21).

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Storage is decentralised: by the economic operator responsible for creating the passport or by DPP service providers authorised to act for it (ESPR Art. 11(c); Batteries Art. 78(c); toys Art. 20(5); detergents Art. 22; CPR Art. 78(c)). ESPR adds a back-up copy made available through a DPP service provider when the product is placed on the market (Art. 10(4)), of the most up-to-date version (Arts 27(1)(c), 29(2)(c)), and Annex III point (l) lets the passport carry the reference of the provider hosting the back-up; the registry checks the link to that back-up where relevant (2026/1778, Art. 8(7)). Toys and detergents copy the back-up duty (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 19(13); Regulation (EU) 2026/405, Art. 21); the Batteries Regulation has no back-up duty and no service-provider concept (battery FAQ Q10.3). Availability: at least the expected lifetime of the product as the delegated act sets (ESPR Art. 9(2)(i)), including after insolvency, liquidation or cessation of Union activity (Art. 11(e); Batteries Art. 78(e)); digital instructions downloadable and online for the expected lifetime and at least 10 years (ESPR Art. 27(7)); toys 10 years after placing on the market (Art. 19(2)(g)); detergents 10 years (Art. 21); construction products: the system stays accessible 25 years after the last product of a type is placed on the market and operators keep passports for at least 10 years (CPR Art. 75(2)(i)). A battery passport ceases to exist after the battery is recycled (Batteries Art. 77(8)). The registry keeps registration data 10 years after registration unless Union law sets the passport availability period (2026/1778, Art. 10(3)). The M/604 draft annex (Part B point 6) asked for decentralised storage, archiving of historical passport data for market surveillance, and persistence after the operator is no longer active; EN 18221:2026 is the cited result (bibliographic only).

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.observable_black_box: Repeated retrievals over time (availability, unchanged identity); presence of a back-up provider reference in the passport; agreement of the primary and back-up copies. Lifetime availability cannot be proven by a finite number of observations.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Access is tiered by actor. ESPR: free and easy access for customers, manufacturers, importers, distributors, dealers, repairers, independent operators, refurbishers, remanufacturers, recyclers, market surveillance and customs authorities, civil society organisations, trade unions and the Commission according to their access rights (Art. 11(b)); the delegated act decides which actors access which data and who may create or update which data (Art. 9(2)(f)-(g)); rights to introduce, modify or update data are restricted accordingly (Art. 11(f)); no personal data of customers without explicit consent under Art. 6 GDPR (Art. 10(1)(e)); a high level of security and privacy and fraud avoidance (Art. 11(h)). Batteries: three tiers fixed in Art. 77(2) and Annex XIII (public: point 1; notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission: points 2 and 3; persons with a legitimate interest: points 2 and 4); access is free of charge per Annex XIII and the Art. 77(9) act (Art. 78(b), (f)); the Art. 77(9) implementing act that defines persons with a legitimate interest and their download, share, publish and re-use rights is not adopted; the battery FAQ says it will not fix the authentication mechanism (Q6.4). Toys and detergents: no registration or password for consumers; no tracking or analysis of use beyond what presentation strictly needs (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 20(4), (10); Regulation (EU) 2026/405, Arts 19, 22). Construction products: access levels in the passport system and protection of trade secrets and intellectual property (CPR Arts 75(2)(b)-(c), 78(f)-(g)). Registry: only the Commission, competent national authorities and customs have access by right (ESPR Art. 13(6)); economic operators and value chain actors use it only after verification (2026/1778, Arts 4-6); each Member State appoints a designated national administrator by 2027-02-18 (Art. 7). The M/604 draft annex (Part B point 3) asked for attribute-based access control, operator responsibility for access rights, product-group-specific rights, no access management for public data, and rules for transferring responsibilities and access rights between operators; EN 18239:2026 is published but not cited in the OJ (bibliographic only).

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.observable_black_box: What each probed role receives on each channel; whether the public tier needs a login; whether restricted fields leak to anonymous requests; tracking requests or cookies on the public view (toys, detergents).

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: The law states outcomes without mechanisms: data authentication, reliability and integrity must be ensured (ESPR Art. 11(g); Batteries Art. 78(g); toys Art. 20(8); detergents Art. 22; CPR Art. 78(h)), with a high level of security and privacy and fraud avoided. The Commission may adopt implementing acts on procedures to issue and verify digital credentials of economic operators and other actors with access rights (ESPR Art. 11, fourth subparagraph); none located. Concrete mechanisms exist only at the registry: operator verification with qualified electronic signatures, qualified electronic seals, electronic identification at assurance level high or (qualified) electronic attestations of attributes, valid until the means expire and at most three years (2026/1778, Arts 4(1)-(4), 5(1)-(4)); a proof of registration that holds the unique product identifier, commodity code where relevant, the responsible operator, the registration date and time of the latest version validated by a Commission electronic time stamp, and a hash of the passport version, guaranteed by a qualified electronic seal under Art. 38 of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 and available for 90 calendar days from generation (Art. 9); 'hash of a passport version' is the cryptographic output generated from that version's data, with no algorithm named (Art. 2(16)); immutable and confidential logs (Art. 14). Non-binding: the user guide's enrolment flow has the legal representative sign or seal a Commission-sealed PDF declaration in PAdES Baseline B, T, LT or LTA with a qualified seal (legal person) or qualified signature (natural person) created on a qualified device or qualified remote service; software .p12/.pfx certificates are rejected; the certificate subject must carry organizationName (OID 2.5.4.10), countryName (2.5.4.6) and organizationIdentifier (2.5.4.97), or givenName (2.5.4.42), surname (2.5.4.4), countryName and serialNumber (2.5.4.5). The M/604 draft annex (Part B point 7) asked for open methods to verify data originality and integrity offline and online, including identifier verification, verifier logs, authentication solutions and verifiable credentials; EN 18246:2026 is published but not cited (bibliographic only).

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.observable_black_box: From a passport alone, law gives no verifiable integrity artifact. An operator-supplied proof of registration can be checked: seal validity, time stamp, and whether its hash matches the passport version observed (once the hash input and algorithm are known).

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: ESPR Art. 13: by 19 July 2026 the Commission sets up a registry that securely stores at least the unique identifiers, the commodity code for products released for free circulation, and the battery unique identifiers of Batteries Art. 77(3); delegated acts may add data (Art. 13(2)); the economic operator placing on the market or putting into service uploads the data (Art. 13(4)); the registry automatically returns a unique registration identifier, which is not proof of compliance (Art. 13(5)); the Commission, competent national authorities and customs have access (Art. 13(6)). Batteries Art. 77(10): the operator uploads the battery unique identifier. Toys Art. 22 and detergents Art. 24: upload product and operator identifiers before placing on the market. CPR Art. 79(2)-(3) applies ESPR Arts 13 and 14. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 sets nine components (secure interface, API, verification platform, registration-identifier scheme, storage of identifiers and commodity codes, list of verified service providers, semantic repository, log system, identification and authorisation schemes; Art. 3); scope covers ESPR products, batteries, construction products, toys, detergents and any other product with a Union passport duty (Art. 1(1)); 'digital product passport' includes the battery passport for this act (Art. 2). Registration flow (Art. 8): verified operator submits at the required granularity; automatic checks of semantic conformity, consistency of mandatory data with the passport, granularity, commodity code validity, and the back-up link; generation and storage of a persistent registration identifier; storage of identifiers, commodity code, service-provider reference, registrant data, date and time and passport integrity evidence; return of the identifier through the same channel. Proof of registration (Art. 9), versioning and retention (Art. 10), semantic repository (Arts 11-12), helpdesk 08:00-20:00 and a 24-hour support tool by February 2029 (Art. 13), logs with retention six months (access), five years (administrative, data exchange) and registration lifetime (modifications) (Art. 14), availability and outage records for at least five years (Art. 15), fraud and massive downloads (Art. 17). Customs (ESPR Art. 15): the declarant gives customs the registration identifier for products under an Art. 4 delegated act; customs release only after verifying that identifier and commodity code against the registry, automatically through the CSW-CERTEX interconnection, which must be operational within four years of the registry act's entry into force (computed 2030-08-06); release is not proof of compliance. Toys Art. 23 and detergents Art. 25 copy this (detergents: automated from 2029-09-23 or the interconnection, whichever is later). The battery FAQ (Q4.1) says the battery registration identifier must not be entered in the customs declaration. Non-binding registry practice: see L01 and L04 (UPI rules, file upload, statuses, error codes, test environment).

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Data must be accurate, complete and up to date (ESPR Art. 9(1); Batteries Art. 77(4); toys Art. 19(2)(d); detergents Art. 21). Delegated acts set who may create or update data and how (ESPR Art. 9(2)(g)-(h)). A new passport for a product that already has one must link to the original passport or passports (ESPR Art. 11(d); toys Art. 20(6); detergents Art. 22). Batteries: the placing operator may authorise another operator in writing (Art. 77(4)); after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing, responsibility passes to the operator that places the resulting battery on the market, which issues a new passport linked to the original one or ones; on becoming waste, responsibility passes to the producer, the producer responsibility organisation or the selected waste management operator (Art. 77(7)); the passport carries a status value (Annex XIII point 4(c)) and new markings show the status change (Art. 13(9)); the passport ends after recycling (Art. 77(8)). Registry: every creation, modification or deletion of registration data is logged and shown in the registration status; versioning with a Commission time stamp per update (2026/1778, Art. 10); a registered passport can be transferred to another verified operator or value chain actor that takes over the obligations from a stated date (Art. 6a); when an operator's verification lapses, it cannot register or change data and statuses are updated (Arts 4(4), 5(4)); recital 1 lets national authorities update or change a passport's status after their own checks. The registry act names no status values; the user guide shows request statuses only (PROCESSING, SUCCESS, FAILURE).

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Economic operators are the manufacturer, authorised representative, importer, distributor, dealer and fulfilment service provider; DPP service providers are not economic operators (ESPR Art. 2(46)). A DPP service provider is an independent third party authorised by the operator placing the product on the market that processes passport data to make it available to actors with access rights (Art. 2(32)); it may not sell, re-use or process the data beyond the service unless specifically agreed (Art. 11, second subparagraph; Batteries Art. 78(d)); requirements and possibly a certification scheme for providers await a delegated act (Art. 11, third subparagraph; Commission timeline Q2 or Q3 2027); the registry keeps a list of verified service providers (2026/1778, Art. 3(f)). Issuing agencies for identifiers are foreseen by Art. 12(4)-(6) (no act located). Duties by role: manufacturer and importer ensure the passport and back-up exist (Arts 27(1)(c), 29(2)(c)); these manufacturer duties cannot be delegated to an authorised representative (Art. 28(1), per the 2026-10-13 audit); distributors verify the link to the passport (Art. 30(2)(a)); dealers make the passport easily accessible including at a distance (Art. 31(2)). Batteries: the operator placing the battery on the market is responsible; the Regulation has no service-provider concept (battery FAQ Q10.3). Public bodies: the Commission sets up and controls the registry and its personal data processing (ESPR Art. 13(1), (3); 2026/1778, Art. 21), maintains the semantic repository (Art. 12), the web portal (ESPR Art. 14) and the CSW-CERTEX link (Art. 15(3)); Member States appoint national administrators and own any connected national components (2026/1778, Arts 7, 22); market surveillance authorities and customs enforce (FAQ Q30-Q31). Presumption of conformity flows from cited harmonised standards (ESPR Art. 41(2)); the Commission FAQ says there is currently no general third-party certification of passport content (Q25).

end_to_end_flows.name: ESPR product placed on the market (once an Art. 4 delegated act applies)
steps: 1. The operator compiles the passport data set that the delegated act requires, using the Commission data model in the semantic repository (ESPR Art. 9(2)(a); 2026/1778, Art. 11).
2. It assigns a persistent unique product identifier at the required granularity and, where needed, operator and facility identifiers (ESPR Arts 10(1)(a), 12).
3. It hosts the passport itself or through a DPP service provider and makes a back-up copy available through a DPP service provider (Arts 10(4), 11(c)).
4. It affixes the data carrier to the product, packaging or documents as the delegated act specifies (Art. 10(1)(b)).
5. It obtains verified status in the registry with eIDAS means (2026/1778, Art. 4) and registers the passport by form, file or API (Art. 8(6)).
6. The registry checks semantic conformity, granularity, commodity code and the back-up link, then returns a persistent registration identifier (Art. 8(7)-(10)).
7. For imports, the declarant gives customs the registration identifier; customs verify it and the commodity code against the registry before release (ESPR Art. 15).
8. On request, the operator gives dealers and marketplaces a digital copy of the carrier or identifier within five working days (Art. 10(3)).
9. A customer scans the carrier, follows the web link and reads the public part; authorities and other actors read restricted parts per their access rights (Arts 2(30), 11(b)).
10. The operator keeps the data accurate; updates are versioned in the registry; a later passport links to the original (Arts 9(1), 11(d); 2026/1778, Art. 10).
11. The passport and its back-up stay available for the required period, also after insolvency or cessation (Art. 11(e)).

end_to_end_flows.name: Battery passport (LMT, industrial above 2 kWh, EV) from 2027-02-18
actors: economic operator placing the battery on the market
notified bodies, market surveillance authorities, Commission
producer, PRO or waste management operator
steps: 1. The operator attributes a unique identifier compliant with ISO/IEC 15459-1 to -6 or equivalent (bibliographic) and links it to the passport (Batteries Art. 77(3)).
2. It marks the battery with a QR code meeting Annex VI Part C that gives access to the passport (Art. 13(6)-(7)).
3. It populates Annex XIII data in three access tiers; items whose source acts are not yet applicable are omitted (Art. 77(2); Annex XIII).

4. It uploads the unique identifier to the ESPR registry (Art. 77(10)); per the user guide this is an item-level registration with an https UPI. As of 2026-09-16 successful battery registration was not yet possible (semantic catalogue not defined).
5. Public data is open to all; restricted data goes to authorities and to persons with a legitimate interest, whose definition awaits the Art. 77(9) implementing act.
6. After repurposing or remanufacturing, the new placing operator issues a new passport linked to the original and the status value changes (Art. 77(7); Annex XIII point 4(c)).
7. When the battery becomes waste, responsibility passes to the producer, PRO or waste management operator; after recycling the passport ceases to exist (Art. 77(7)-(8)).

end_to_end_flows.name: Registry enrolment and registration (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 with the user guide v1.03)
steps: 1. The user signs in through EU Login and creates an organisation application (legal or natural person; identifier type such as NTR or TIN).
2. The legal representative's name and email are entered; the registry generates a Commission-sealed PDF declaration.
3. The representative seals (QSeal) or signs (QES) the PDF in PAdES Baseline B, T, LT or LTA; subject attributes must match the application data.
4. The signed PDF is uploaded and submitted; the application status appears in the Activity Dashboard; on success the user becomes organisation administrator.

5. The user selects the product group, granularity and enters the UPI (https URL, at most 2000 characters) with optional model and batch identifiers, or uploads a JSON or XML file of up to 100 passports.
6. The request gets a correlation ID and the status PROCESSING; the registry validates schema, uniqueness, URL rules, UPI resolvability and semantics.
7. On SUCCESS the registration detail lists UPI, registration identifier ('URI') and product group; on FAILURE it lists each UPI with an error; one error rejects the whole file.
8. The operator can generate a proof of registration (qualified seal, Commission time stamp, passport-version hash), valid for 90 calendar days (Art. 9).

end_to_end_flows.name: Toy or detergent passport (sectoral acts reusing ESPR infrastructure)
steps: 1. The manufacturer creates a model-level passport with at least Annex VI Part I (toys) or Part A (detergents) data before placing on the market (toys Art. 19(1)-(2); detergents Art. 21).
2. It links the passport through a carrier to a persistent unique product identifier and uses ESPR identifier rules (toys Art. 21; detergents Art. 23).
3. It uploads product and operator identifiers to the ESPR registry and receives a registration identifier (toys Art. 22; detergents Art. 24).
4. Consumers access it free, without registration or password, without tracking beyond need (toys Art. 20(4), (10); detergents Art. 22).
5. The passport and a back-up copy stay available for 10 years (toys Art. 19(2)(g), (13); detergents Art. 21). Application: toys from 2030-08-01; detergents from 2029-09-23.

failure_modes.fault: Carrier encodes a bare GTIN or serial number instead of a URL, so no web link exists.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Parse the decoded payload as an https URL; resolution impossible.

failure_modes.fault: UPI uses http:// or a non-default port, so the registry rejects it ('The UPI URL is invalid').
failure_modes.detectable_by: Syntax check of the payload against the https-url profile.

failure_modes.fault: Two products or two entries in one registration file share a UPI.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Duplicate detection over a registration file or a sample of carriers.

failure_modes.fault: UPI redirects through http or through a long redirect chain, so registry validation fails as not resolvable.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Record the redirect chain and schemes during bounded resolution.

failure_modes.fault: Public passport sits behind a login wall or a cookie wall.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Anonymous fetch returns 401, 403 or an HTML login page instead of passport content.

failure_modes.fault: Restricted Annex XIII points 2-4 appear in the public JSON, in search results or in error messages.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Canary-based leak search on all channels for role anonymous.

failure_modes.fault: Passport view loads analytics or third-party trackers (toys, detergents).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Record cookies and third-party requests of the HTML view.

failure_modes.fault: Mandatory public battery fields missing, or fields filled that are not yet applicable (for example carbon footprint before its act applies) with placeholder values.
Passport served only as a PDF or an HTML page, not as structured machine-readable data.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Media type and parse check of the response.

failure_modes.fault: Back-up copy at the service provider is stale or missing; or the passport names no back-up provider.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare primary and back-up documents; check the provider reference field.

failure_modes.fault: Passport disappears when the operator's domain lapses.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Scheduled acquisitions show loss of availability; back-up still reachable or not.

failure_modes.fault: Proof of registration expired (older than 90 days) or its hash no longer matches the current passport version after an unregistered update.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate seal time and hash against the observed version (once the hash method is known).

failure_modes.fault: Registration made at batch level although the product-group rule requires item level, or item registration lacks the batch and model links.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Granularity rules over the registration file or export.

failure_modes.fault: Remanufactured battery gets a fresh passport without a link to the original, or keeps status 'original'.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Predecessor-link check and status enumeration check.

failure_modes.fault: Passport of a recycled battery still answers as active.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Status field 'waste' plus continued availability after declared recycling (manual evidence of recycling needed).

open_questions: Which access rules apply to Annex XIII points 2 and 4 on 2027-02-18 if the Art. 77(9) implementing act is still not adopted?

What hash algorithm and which input (canonical form of which passport version) does the registry use for the 'hash of a passport version' in the proof of registration (2026/1778, Arts 2(16), 9)? What is the file format of the proof?
When will the registry API specification ('DPP Registry technical guidelines') and the semantic repository's public APIs be published, and at which URLs?
Does 'the UPI must resolve' mean an HTTP 200 with passport data, and which media types, redirect limits, ports and domains does the registry allow? The guide names the rules but not the values.

Do the OJ citations of EN 18219:2026 and EN 18220:2026 end the ESPR fallback to the ISO/IEC 15459 series (Arts 10(1)(c), 12(1)), and from which date? The Batteries Regulation keeps its own reference (Art. 77(3)).
Is the battery passport subject to the ESPR back-up duty (Art. 10(4))? No provision applies it; the battery FAQ (Q10.3) says the Batteries Regulation has no service-provider concept.
Is registration a precondition for placing a battery on the market from 2027-02-18, given that the guide says battery registration is not yet possible?
How is 'five working days' (ESPR Art. 10(3)) counted across Member States with different public holidays?
Which status values will the registry use for a registered passport (2026/1778, Art. 10 names none) and how does a national authority's status change (recital 1) appear to the operator?
Does the toy regulation's Art. 19 apply only from 2030-08-01 (Art. 59), while Art. 49 delegated powers apply from 2026-01-01? The DPP FAQ table says DPP delegated powers apply from 1 January 2026.
